_comment: Layer 0: the civilization imbalance map. Maintained and audited BEFORE any company is scored. The imbalance must exist independently of any company; a company can only attach to a correction that is already established here.
_premise: Treat Homo sapiens the way an ecologist studying any species would: measure population, energy use, resource flows, waste streams, habitat modification, cooperation, competition and the feedback loops of its tools. Civilization is a metabolism. Money is not the underlying system; it is an information layer coordinating access to energy, matter, labor, land and time. The engine's first question is therefore not about companies at all: where is the metabolism of Homo sapiens furthest from a stable regenerative state?

_forms.overshoot: human throughput exceeds the regenerative or assimilative capacity of the surrounding system
_forms.deficit: the system fails to provide an essential human need adequately despite consuming substantial resources
_forms.bridge: the future lies where both fall at once: more human need satisfied with less energy, material extraction, waste, scarcity and ecological disruption

_hierarchy: MEASURED CORRECTION PER DOLLAR OF REVENUE

_severity.formula: severity index = distance x load x rate x exposure x irreversibility, on an open instrument with a ceiling of 486. The ceiling is deliberately lethal: it would mean a load-bearing global stock past a hard limit for the species, effectively permanent, and still diverging fast. Nothing on the map is near it, which is the point; the top of the scale is reserved for readings that would actually mean the species cannot live there.

anchors.distance: for an overshoot, the ratio of the control variable to its boundary: 0 inside the safe range, 1 at the edge, 2 outside but under 2x, 3 between 2x and 10x, 4 between 10x and 100x, 5 beyond 100x, 6 past a known hard limit for the species. For a deficit, the share of the species without the essential: 0 none, 1 under 5 percent, 2 up to a quarter, 3 up to three quarters, 4 above three quarters, 5 essentially universal deprivation, 6 the need cannot be met at all
anchors.load: 1 to 3: how load-bearing the stock is for the biosphere or for civilization
anchors.rate: 0.5 returning toward the safe range, 1 holding its distance, 2 diverging, 3 diverging fast; a return halves severity rather than zeroing it, because distance still exists while the stock travels back
anchors.irreversibility: 1 reversible in years, 2 decades, 3 centuries or effectively permanent

_severity.note: the exact calculation is expected to evolve as evidence accumulates; what is fixed is the separation of STATE, MOVEMENT, FLOW, COUNTERFORCE, CORRECTION, CLOCK and COMPANIES, in that order, and that movement is stated as position relative to the safe range, never as better or worse

_hypothesis.name: the convergence hypothesis
_hypothesis.statement: as technological capability increases, does civilization systematically move toward greater abundance of essential outcomes while requiring less scarce material, energy and human labor per outcome?
mechanisms: AI lowers the cost of intelligence and coordination
automation lowers the labor required per unit of production
renewable and advanced energy systems lower the resource cost of usable energy
precision agriculture and biological systems lower inputs per unit of nutrition
closed-loop manufacturing lowers virgin material demand
distributed production lowers transportation and coordination requirements
preventive and regenerative medicine lowers the resources required to maintain health
_hypothesis.status: a falsifiable hypothesis, not a promise; the tracked portfolio is one running test of it, and it is allowed to fail

_rule: Do not predict the future by extrapolating markets. Measure the imbalance, determine the direction the physical system must move to resolve it, measure the clock, then find the mechanisms carrying civilization in that direction. The crystal ball is not a prediction. The crystal ball is the distance from equilibrium.
_sources: Planetary boundaries: Richardson et al. 2023 and the 2025 Planetary Health Check (seven of nine processes outside the safe range). Provisioning: WHO/UNICEF JMP, FAO SOFI 2024, Tracking SDG7 2024, WHO UHC 2023, ITU 2024, UN-Habitat, Circularity Gap Report. Figures are order-of-scale and dated in each entry; they are inputs to be re-researched, not constants.

systems.name: Atmospheric greenhouse gases
systems.stock: carbon dioxide and other heat-trapping gases accumulated in the atmosphere
systems.safe_range: 350 ppm CO2 or below (planetary boundary; pre-industrial was 280)
systems.state: about 425 ppm CO2 (2024-2025 annual mean), rising 2 to 3 ppm per year
systems.distance_note: 75 ppm past the boundary and moving away from it; the fastest sustained rise in the ice-core record
systems.cause: fossil fuel combustion for energy and transport, plus land clearing that turns standing carbon into emitted carbon
systems.correction: substitute non-fossil energy for fossil flows, electrify end uses, cut energy lost per useful outcome, stop land-carbon loss and rebuild sinks
systems.clock: decades; the energy capital stock turns over on a 20 to 40 year cycle and the gas itself persists for centuries
systems.envelope: CO2 breathed between 180 and 300 ppm through every glacial cycle of the last 800,000 years of ice cores; the current excursion is outside that envelope in level and roughly 100x outside it in speed

counterforce.mechanisms: damage-cost feedback through insurance and disaster losses, policy and legal pressure; the natural sinks absorb roughly half the flow but weaken as they warm
counterforce.alternatives: substitutes at or below cost parity and scaling: solar, wind and storage on compounding learning curves, electrified end uses
counterforce.evidence: solar and battery costs fell about 90 percent in a decade, making new clean electricity the cheapest in history; every further ppm strengthens the damage signal that funds the substitution

systems.name: Biological diversity
systems.stock: living species and the genetic library they carry
systems.safe_range: under 10 extinctions per million species-years (the background rate is roughly 1)
systems.state: above 100 extinctions per million species-years, at least ten times the boundary
systems.distance_note: an order of magnitude past the boundary; each loss is permanent on any human timescale
systems.cause: habitat conversion for food and settlement, overharvesting, chemical and nutrient load, climate shift
systems.correction: shrink the land, sea and chemical footprint per unit of human need met, so habitat and populations can be returned faster than they are taken
systems.clock: decades to begin, centuries to recover; extinction itself never reverses
systems.envelope: background extinction runs near 0.1 to 1 E/MSY, punctuated by rare pulses; the die-off arm of the rhythm is real, but the current rate is a sustained pulse, not a beat

counterforce.mechanisms: no automatic price on extinction; policy commitments and liability, none of it self-strengthening
counterforce.alternatives: no substitute exists for a species; restoration works only where habitat and time are given back, and both remain scarce
counterforce.evidence: extinction carries no price signal, so the counterforce must be built by policy rather than emerging from the excursion itself; this is the map's furthest-out stock with its weakest spring

systems.name: Available biological productivity
systems.stock: net primary production, the yearly plant growth every other species also lives on
systems.safe_range: human appropriation below about 10 percent of net primary production
systems.state: human appropriation of net primary production is roughly 30 percent

control.variable: human appropriation of net primary production

systems.distance_note: about three times the boundary; what one species takes, every other food web loses
systems.cause: cropland and pasture expansion, biomass harvest, and the losses between harvest and actual human nutrition
systems.correction: more nutrition per hectare and per tonne of biomass: higher-efficiency protein, waste-stream recovery, precision inputs, land returned to wild productivity
systems.clock: decades; land use changes at the speed of food systems
systems.envelope: no single species in the record has held a third of land plant growth; there is no known oscillation that returns this appropriation on its own

counterforce.mechanisms: land scarcity raises the return on every efficiency
counterforce.alternatives: precision agriculture, efficient protein conversion and waste-stream recovery: deployable now, approaching cost parity
counterforce.evidence: the dearer land becomes, the more intensification and sparing pay; precision agriculture adoption tracks input prices

systems.name: Forests and habitat
systems.stock: standing forest and connected wild habitat
systems.safe_range: at least 75 percent of original forest cover standing
systems.state: about 60 percent of original forest cover remains
systems.distance_note: 15 points below the boundary, with tropical loss still running ahead of regrowth
systems.cause: clearing for agriculture and settlement, logging, fire regimes shifted by climate
systems.correction: agricultural intensity that frees land, materials that substitute for virgin timber, and regrowth protected long enough to become forest again
systems.clock: decades to stop the loss, a century or more to regrow what was primary
systems.envelope: forests burn, die and regrow on decades to centuries, and cover stayed inside that envelope until net conversion began outrunning regrowth

counterforce.mechanisms: payments for standing forest remain small; the loss is priced almost nowhere
counterforce.alternatives: engineered substitutes for virgin timber and yield gains that spare land exist, and regrowth is automatic wherever pressure lifts
counterforce.evidence: regrowth works wherever pressure lifts, but the payments that would couple the counterforce to the loss remain small

systems.name: Freshwater and groundwater
systems.stock: rivers, soil moisture and aquifers in their historical envelopes
systems.safe_range: streamflow and soil-moisture deviations on no more land than the pre-industrial baseline; aquifers drawn no faster than recharge
systems.state: both surface and soil water crossed their boundary in the 2023 assessment; a majority of the largest aquifers are being drawn down faster than they refill
systems.distance_note: the land area seeing major water-cycle deviation runs about double its baseline
systems.cause: irrigation drawing more than recharge, watershed disruption, contamination, and a warming atmosphere moving water differently
systems.correction: reuse, leakage reduction, treatment, desalination where appropriate, efficient irrigation, watershed regeneration
systems.clock: years for efficiency and reuse; decades to centuries for a depleted aquifer
systems.envelope: rivers and soil moisture swing with seasons and decades; deep aquifers refill on centuries to millennia, so drawdown there sits outside any usable rhythm

counterforce.mechanisms: pumping cost rises as the table falls, an automatic scarcity price
counterforce.alternatives: reuse, drip irrigation, leak detection and desalination, all deployable at known cost
counterforce.evidence: every metre of drawdown raises the energy cost per litre, which is the aquifer's own hunger signal

systems.name: Fertile soil
systems.stock: topsoil depth, soil carbon and soil biology
systems.safe_range: erosion at or below soil formation, which runs on the order of a centimetre per century
systems.state: roughly a third of agricultural land is degraded; erosion on tilled land commonly runs 10 to 100 times formation
systems.distance_note: losing in decades what forms in centuries
systems.cause: tillage, bare ground, compaction, salinization, and nutrient mining without return flows
systems.correction: farming that keeps soil covered and living, nutrient return instead of nutrient mining, and yield gains that retire fragile land
systems.clock: decades to stabilize, centuries to rebuild depth
systems.envelope: under cover, formation and erosion trade places within a narrow band; the current loss rate has no return arm on a human timescale

counterforce.mechanisms: yield decline on degraded ground arrives as farm-level cost within years
counterforce.alternatives: cover cropping, no-till and precision inputs: known, cheap and spreading
counterforce.evidence: degradation is self-advertising to the person who farms it, on a lag of years rather than centuries

systems.name: Nitrogen and phosphorus loads
systems.stock: reactive nitrogen and phosphorus moving through soils and waters
systems.safe_range: about 62 Tg of newly fixed nitrogen and 11 Tg of phosphorus flow per year
systems.state: roughly 190 Tg of nitrogen fixed and about 22 Tg of phosphorus flowing per year, two to three times the boundaries
systems.distance_note: dead zones downstream of farmland are the visible edge of the overload
systems.cause: fertilizer applied beyond crop uptake, concentrated animal waste, and sewage returned to water instead of land
systems.correction: precision application, recovery of nutrients from waste streams back into the food loop, and treatment before discharge
systems.clock: years to a decade; nutrient practice changes as fast as farm economics allow
systems.envelope: biological nitrogen fixation held a stable ceiling for the whole Holocene; industry now fixes roughly twice what all natural processes combined do

counterforce.mechanisms: past crop uptake every extra kilogram is nearly pure cost, and dead zones attract liability
counterforce.alternatives: precision application and nutrient recovery from waste streams, deployable now
counterforce.evidence: past crop uptake, every extra kilogram is nearly pure cost; precision application pays for itself faster the higher prices go

systems.name: Ocean chemistry
systems.stock: the carbonate chemistry that shell-forming ocean life is built on
systems.safe_range: aragonite saturation at or above 80 percent of its pre-industrial level
systems.state: surface ocean about 30 percent more acidic than pre-industrial; the 2025 assessment marks this boundary crossed, the seventh of nine
systems.distance_note: just past the edge and tracking CO2 upward
systems.cause: the ocean absorbing roughly a quarter of fossil CO2 emissions
systems.correction: the same correction as the atmosphere: cut the CO2 flow; the ocean has no separate lever
systems.clock: centuries; deep-ocean chemistry mixes on a millennial clock
systems.envelope: surface pH swung this far before, over millennia on glacial cycles; the current swing of similar size took 150 years

counterforce.mechanisms: no lever of its own; the pressure is the atmosphere's
counterforce.alternatives: no direct alternative exists; the ocean's access is the energy transition's access, on a millennial lag
counterforce.evidence: inherits whatever the CO2 counterforce achieves; deep-ocean chemistry then follows on a millennial lag

systems.name: Persistent chemicals and synthetic materials
systems.stock: synthetic compounds and plastics accumulating in living tissue, soil and water
systems.safe_range: release no faster than assessment and breakdown; formally, a boundary crossed when production outruns evaluation
systems.state: hundreds of thousands of registered synthetics and about 460 Mt of plastic per year, produced far faster than safety is assessed
systems.distance_note: marked outside its boundary since 2022; the magnitude itself is unquantified, which is part of the problem
systems.cause: single-pass material design: produced, used briefly, dispersed
systems.correction: closed loops for what exists, destruction and containment of the worst of it, and material design that can re-enter either biology or industry
systems.clock: decades; persistence is the defining property
systems.envelope: no natural envelope exists; these compounds have no evolutionary history at all

counterforce.mechanisms: liability and litigation that scale with discovered harm
counterforce.alternatives: destruction, containment and green chemistry exist but remain immature at scale
counterforce.evidence: the longer a persistent compound accumulates, the larger the liability attached to it; the counterforce arrives late but compounds

systems.name: Recoverable material stocks
systems.stock: metals, minerals and biomass held in forms that can actually be recovered and reused
systems.safe_range: extraction paced so that secondary supply can meet most demand
systems.state: global extraction is around 100 Gt per year and the share cycled back is about 7 percent and falling

control.variable: share of material input cycled back

systems.distance_note: the boundary here is a working target (the Circularity Gap baseline), not a planetary constant
systems.cause: virgin extraction priced below recovery, products designed against disassembly, collection loops missing
systems.correction: deposit and return systems, recovery infrastructure, design for disassembly, and secondary material made cheaper than virgin
systems.clock: years to decades; loops are built at industrial speed once the economics flip
systems.envelope: geology concentrates ores on timescales with no human rhythm; the usable envelope here is the loop civilization builds, not one nature provides

counterforce.mechanisms: declining ore grades raise the cost of every virgin tonne
counterforce.alternatives: recycling, deposit-return and design for disassembly are proven; secondary supply scales wherever collection exists
counterforce.evidence: every tonne of easy ore mined makes the recycled tonne relatively cheaper

systems.name: Stratospheric ozone
systems.stock: the ozone layer screening surface life from UV-B
systems.safe_range: less than 5 percent below the 1980 column
systems.state: back inside its boundary and healing; Antarctic recovery is projected around the 2060s
systems.distance_note: the recovered control: one global correction that was actually completed
systems.cause: was CFC release; the Montreal Protocol cut the flow and the stock is refilling
systems.correction: hold the phase-out; nothing new required
systems.clock: on track; full recovery by roughly 2066
systems.envelope: back inside the envelope it left; the excursion took about fifty years going out and is taking about eighty coming back

counterforce.mechanisms: treaty pressure, held in place
counterforce.alternatives: substitutes for CFCs existed at comparable cost, which is why this flip could be managed rather than suffered
counterforce.evidence: the spring has already released; this row is what a completed flip looks like

systems.name: Nutritious food
systems.stock: people adequately nourished, and the reserve between harvests and need
systems.safe_range: essentially no one chronically undernourished; the food system inside the land, water and nutrient boundaries it draws on
systems.state: about 733 million people undernourished and 2.3 billion food-insecure (2024), while the food system is the largest single driver of the land, water and nutrient overshoots above
systems.distance_note: the sharpest case of both failures at once: overshoot in inputs, deficit in outcomes
systems.cause: calories and nutrients lost between field and person, purchasing power gaps, conflict, and yield systems leaning on depleting inputs
systems.correction: more nutrition delivered per unit of land, water, nitrogen and money: efficient protein, waste-stream recovery, resilient low-cost distribution
systems.clock: years; food flows respond fast when cost per nutritious calorie falls

counterforce.mechanisms: hunger is the oldest pressure there is, but it couples weakly to market pull where incomes are lowest
counterforce.alternatives: efficient protein, recovered waste streams and low-cost distribution, deployable now
counterforce.evidence: the counterforce is strong where purchasing power exists and weakly coupled where it does not; the hungriest exert the least market pull, which is why this deficit persists beside abundance

systems.name: Potable water
systems.stock: people with safely managed drinking water
systems.safe_range: universal access
systems.state: about 2.2 billion people without safely managed drinking water (JMP)
systems.distance_note: the gap closes every year, but a quarter of the species remains outside
systems.cause: missing treatment and distribution, contamination, and source depletion pricing water out of reach
systems.correction: treatment, leakage reduction, reuse, and metering that makes the losses visible
systems.clock: years to a decade at current build rates

counterforce.mechanisms: waterborne disease and hauling time press constantly on the unserved
counterforce.alternatives: treatment and desalination at known, falling cost; metering that finds the losses
counterforce.evidence: desalinated water now clears at well under a dollar a cubic metre where energy is cheap

systems.name: Shelter
systems.stock: adequate dwellings reachable at ordinary incomes
systems.safe_range: essentially no one in unsafe or unaffordable housing
systems.state: about 1.1 billion people live in informal settlements, and the cost of an adequate dwelling is diverging from ordinary incomes inside wealthy countries too
systems.distance_note: a deficit produced mostly by cost per unit, not by absent technology
systems.cause: construction cost and productivity stagnant for decades, land constraints, and building stock that leaks energy
systems.correction: lower cost per adequate dwelling: industrialized construction, higher build productivity, envelopes that cut lifetime energy
systems.clock: years to decades; housing moves at construction speed

counterforce.mechanisms: unaffordability is felt everywhere and widening
counterforce.alternatives: industrialized construction that would cut cost per dwelling barely exists at scale; access, not pressure, is what this deficit lacks
counterforce.evidence: construction productivity has been roughly flat for decades, which is why this deficit persists inside wealthy countries; the weakest provisioning spring on the map

systems.name: Usable energy
systems.stock: people with reliable electricity and clean cooking energy
systems.safe_range: universal access
systems.state: about 685 million people without electricity and 2.1 billion without clean cooking (2024 tracking)
systems.distance_note: progress stalled in the places furthest behind
systems.cause: grid build-out cost, conversion losses, and energy poverty where incomes meet fuel prices
systems.correction: cheaper delivered kilowatt-hours: generation where the demand is, less energy lost in conversion and distribution, metered visibility of the losses
systems.clock: years to a decade; solar plus storage is the fastest provisioning build-out in history

counterforce.mechanisms: energy poverty and fuel cost, felt daily
counterforce.alternatives: solar plus storage at or below parity, distributed so it can skip the grid entirely; the steepest learning curve on the map
counterforce.evidence: cost falls with every doubling of deployment, and deployment is pulled by the deficit itself; the most compressed spring on the map

systems.name: Healthcare capacity
systems.stock: the capacity to prevent, diagnose and treat, per person who needs it
systems.safe_range: essential services reaching everyone without financial ruin
systems.state: about 4.5 billion people not fully covered by essential health services, and 2 billion facing catastrophic or impoverishing health spending (WHO)
systems.distance_note: the deficit is capacity per clinician-hour and cost per outcome, not medical knowledge
systems.cause: care models that spend scarce clinician time and facility capacity late, on complications that earlier and cheaper intervention would have prevented
systems.correction: more health per clinician-hour and per dollar: earlier diagnosis, prevention over rescue, care moved from theatre to bedside to home
systems.clock: years to decades, paced by reimbursement and adoption

counterforce.mechanisms: untreated disease is its own pressure, and late care compounds system cost
counterforce.alternatives: cheap diagnostics, prevention and home care exist; institutions adopt them slowly
counterforce.evidence: sequencing and diagnostic costs collapsed while delivery models moved slowly; the technology spring is loaded, the institutional one is not

systems.name: Sanitation
systems.stock: people with safely managed sanitation, and waste turned back into safe flows
systems.safe_range: universal access, with waste streams treated rather than discharged
systems.state: about 3.5 billion people without safely managed sanitation (JMP)
systems.distance_note: returning toward universal coverage, and every remaining gap feeds directly into the water and nutrient imbalances above
systems.cause: treatment infrastructure missing or overloaded; waste discharged to the same waters people drink
systems.correction: treatment build-out, and recovery of the water, energy and nutrients the waste stream contains
systems.clock: years to a decade at current build rates

counterforce.mechanisms: disease burden and the contamination of the same waters people drink
counterforce.alternatives: treatment build-out at known cost, with resource recovery paying part of the bill
counterforce.evidence: where the recovered water, energy and nutrients are priced, collection funds itself

systems.name: Transportation and access
systems.stock: the ability of people and goods to reach what they need
systems.safe_range: all-weather access for everyone, at energy and material cost the other boundaries can carry
systems.state: about 1 billion rural people lack all-weather road access, while freight runs with roughly a third of trucks moving empty
systems.distance_note: a deficit of access and an overshoot of empty movement at the same time
systems.cause: fragmented logistics, modal choices set by habit rather than energy cost, infrastructure gaps
systems.correction: fewer empty miles, freight shifted to the lowest-energy mode that works, assets kept alive longer
systems.clock: decades; transport stock turns over slowly

counterforce.mechanisms: empty miles are pure cost, and fuel prices press on every route
counterforce.alternatives: logistics software and electric drivetrains, deployable now
counterforce.evidence: the empty-mile share is pure cost, and software that removes it pays immediately

systems.name: Productive tools
systems.stock: the machinery and compute that multiply what one person-hour produces
systems.safe_range: no agreed global control variable exists; the working measure is capability per worker and its cost curve
systems.state: tool capability per worker is rising and its cost is falling on every curve that can be measured, but access remains deeply uneven
systems.distance_note: the softest measurement on this map, and marked as such
systems.cause: capital cost and skills gaps between the tool frontier and most of the species
systems.correction: cheaper capability per unit: compute, automation, and machines that let one operator do the work of several
systems.clock: years; tool cost curves are the fastest-moving on the map

counterforce.mechanisms: the productivity gap is a wage gap, felt person by person
counterforce.alternatives: compute cost collapse and machines that multiply one operator's output; the canonical accessible alternative
counterforce.evidence: capability per dollar has compounded for fifty years without pause

systems.name: Information and knowledge
systems.stock: people connected to the species' shared information layer
systems.safe_range: universal meaningful connectivity
systems.state: about 2.2 billion people remain offline (2024), and the number falls every year
systems.distance_note: the provisioning stock closest to closing
systems.cause: infrastructure and affordability gaps at the edge of the network
systems.correction: cheaper connectivity and cheaper intelligence per person; the substrate is compute
systems.clock: years

counterforce.mechanisms: exclusion from the information layer is exclusion from most modern provisioning
counterforce.alternatives: terrestrial and satellite connectivity falling in cost at once
counterforce.evidence: each doubling of coverage lowers the cost of the next; the offline count falls every year it is measured

systems.name: Resilient infrastructure
systems.stock: the margin between what built systems can absorb and what now hits them
systems.safe_range: maintenance and hardening keeping pace with load and climate exposure
systems.state: weather losses run on the order of 300 billion dollars a year and rising, while deferred maintenance accumulates on bridges, mains and grids built for a milder century
systems.distance_note: the buffer is being spent from both ends: rising load, deferred upkeep
systems.cause: maintenance deferred because it is invisible until failure; exposure rising faster than hardening
systems.correction: repair over replacement, engineering capacity multiplied by software, observability that finds the weak points before they fail
systems.clock: decades; infrastructure moves at the speed of budgets and concrete

counterforce.mechanisms: insurance reprices with every loss year, an automatic bill for the damage signal
counterforce.alternatives: repair-over-replace methods, engineering software leverage and observability, deployable now
counterforce.evidence: premiums are the damage signal arriving as a bill; they rise with every loss year and fund the hardening

_rhythm: Nothing in nature holds still, and the map does not treat movement as failure. Wolves multiply until they outrun the deer; the crash feeds the deer's recovery, which feeds the wolves' recovery. Tree stocks grow, burn, die and regrow. That ebb and flow is what balance looks like, so a safe range here means the envelope a stock's own oscillations have stayed inside for as long as the record runs. A stock inside its envelope is in rhythm however fast it is moving. Imbalance is narrower and checkable: the stock has left its envelope, or is leaving it at a speed the envelope never contained. When that happens the correction still arrives, the way it arrives for the wolves; the only question the engine asks is whether it arrives as a managed return or as the die-off arm of the loop.
_scale_note: None of this is a danger to the planet itself. Planets have no preferred state, and Earth has run far hotter and far colder than anything on this map. The envelope belongs to the species: it is the range that every system Homo sapiens depends on was built inside. Distance is measured from that envelope, and the top of the scale is reserved for readings that would mean the species cannot live there.

_counterforce.doctrine: Whenever a system moves in one direction, the counterforce against that movement gathers as it goes: the wolves' hunger grows with every deer eaten, and the hunger is what flips the momentum. But pressure alone does not decide the flip; access to the alternative does. The counterforce is therefore two measured things: the pressure pushing back, and the reachability of the path the system could take instead. Access decides which arm the correction takes. With an accessible alternative the flip is a managed return; without one it is the die-off arm. The wolves have no second prey, so their correction is a crash. The makers of CFCs had substitutes at comparable cost, so ozone's correction was a treaty. Access is also where technology enters the equation: as general capability rises, AI and automation raise access across many systems at once, which is the convergence hypothesis acting inside the counterforce. If that hypothesis is true, turn pressures across this map should rise over the coming years even where pressure holds still, and the map will show it. The clock in every entry is a reading of the counterforce, not a date pulled from air. This is the company engine's measure C, the loop, applied one level up.
_counterforce.formula: turn pressure = distance x pressure x access x coupling, on an instrument with a ceiling of 108

anchors.pressure: 0 none identified on a human clock; 1 latent or weakly organized; 2 building and measurable; 3 strong and compounding: an automatic price or damage signal already bending the flows
anchors.access: 0 no alternative exists, so the correction can only arrive as the die-off arm; 1 an alternative exists but is immature or costly; 2 deployable and approaching parity; 3 at or below parity and scaling
anchors.coupling: grows (x2): the counterforce strengthens as the excursion deepens; flat (x1): it exists but does not scale with displacement; weakens (x0.5): the excursion erodes its own counterforce
anchors.reading: high distance with high turn pressure is a compressed spring: the flip is near, predictable, and headed for a managed return. High distance with low turn pressure is the dangerous reading: the excursion runs further, and if access is the missing factor, what eventually turns it is the die-off arm
